actions.name: approve_invitation
actions.description: Accepts a pending LinkedIn connection invitation, immediately making the sender a 1st-degree connection and notifying them. This changes state on the user's account, so the user must explicitly approve it before you call it; get invitation_id, validation_token and profile_id from list_invitations read right beforehand.

invitation_id.description: Identifier of the pending invitation to accept, taken from the list_invitations result.

validation_token.description: Single-use validation token for this invitation from a fresh list_invitations call; re-fetch the list if it has already been used or is stale.

profile_id.description: Identifier of the inviting person's LinkedIn profile, as returned by list_invitations for this invitation.

_payload.value: ["Sorry, invitation from Jai not accepted. Please try again."]

actions.name: create_post
actions.description: Publishes a text-only post to the user's LinkedIn feed. This changes state on the user's account and creates a real, public post visible to anyone immediately, so the user must approve it before you call this tool. It cannot attach images, video, links, polls, or @mentions/hashtags, and it returns the new post's URN (urn:li:ugcPost:...).

actions.name: get_company
actions.description: Fetch a LinkedIn company page by its universalName (the slug in linkedin.com/company/<universalName>), returning compact rows for the company plus related organisations such as affiliates and similar pages, with fields like company_urn, name, universal_name, url, tagline, description, employee_count, employee range, website, and industry_urn. This is a read-only operation and is safe to retry; match the returned universal_name against the one requested to identify the target company row.

universal_name.description: The company's universalName: the slug in its LinkedIn page URL (linkedin.com/company/<universalName>), e.g. "microsoft".

actions.name: get_conversation_messages
actions.description: Read the most recent messages in a single LinkedIn conversation thread, returned newest first with text, subject (InMails only), delivery time, and sender details. This is read-only and safe to retry; for older messages, call get_earlier_messages with the oldest delivered_at returned.

conversation_urn.description: Full URN of the conversation thread to read, e.g. urn:li:msg_conversation:(urn:li:fsd_profile:ACoAAE...,2-YTgx...). Obtain it from list_conversations, search_conversations or list_conversations_page.

actions.name: get_earlier_messages
actions.description: LinkedIn: page backward through a conversation's history, returning up to `count` messages sent before a given timestamp (one row per message, same shape as get_conversation_messages); an empty result means you have passed the oldest message. Repeat with before_timestamp set to the oldest delivered_at seen so far to walk a whole thread. Read-only and safe to retry.

conversation_urn.description: URN of the conversation to read, e.g. urn:li:msg_conversation:(urn:li:fsd_profile:ACoAAErYbl4B...,2-YTgxZDMx...); obtain it from list_conversations.

actions.name: get_me
actions.description: Identifies the signed-in LinkedIn member, returning their profile_urn (the 'urn:li:fsd_profile:<id>' to pass as mailbox_urn to list_conversations and send_message), member_urn, first_name, last_name, public_identifier (the /in/ slug), occupation, and premium status. Call this first for any messaging task; it is read-only, takes no parameters, and is safe to retry.

actions.name: get_profile
actions.description: Resolves a LinkedIn public profile vanity name (the '/in/<name>' slug) to the member's profile URN (strip 'urn:li:fsd_profile:' to get the ACoAA… id needed by list_followers), name, headline, premium flag, summary, country code, location and industry URN. Returns only the exact member for that slug, or an empty result if it did not resolve; read-only and safe to retry.

vanity_name.description: The public identifier from a LinkedIn profile URL, i.e. the slug after '/in/' without slashes (e.g. 'williamhgates').

actions.name: get_profile_education
actions.description: Fetches a LinkedIn member's education history, returning one row per entry with school_name, degree_name, field_of_study, start_year, end_year and description, most recent first. This is a read-only operation that changes nothing and is safe to retry.

vanity_name.description: The member's LinkedIn vanity name, the slug after /in/ in their profile URL (e.g. 'williamhgates'), same as used by get_profile.

actions.name: get_profile_experience
actions.description: Fetches a LinkedIn member's work history as one row per position (title, company, company_urn, location, start/end year and month, description), most recent first; a row with no end_year is a current role. Read-only and safe to retry.

vanity_name.description: The member's LinkedIn vanity name, i.e. the <slug> in /in/<slug>, such as 'williamhgates'.

actions.name: list_conversations
actions.description: Lists the LinkedIn member's most recent ~20 message threads (inbox), newest first, with unread counts, participants and the latest message in each; use it as the entry point for reading or replying to messages, and use search_conversations to find a thread by name or keyword, or list_conversations_page then list_conversations_next to go further back. Read-only and safe to retry.

actions.name: list_invitations
actions.description: Lists the member's pending received LinkedIn connection invitations, returning one row per invitation with invitation_id, validation_token, invitation_type (GenericInvitationType_CONNECTION for a person, GenericInvitationType_ORGANIZATION for a company page, which has no profile_id) and profile_id for person invites. This is read-only and safe to retry; call it immediately before approve_invitation or reject_invitation because the id and single-use token are both required and old tokens should not be reused.

actions.name: list_mailboxes
actions.description: Lists the LinkedIn company-page mailboxes the signed-in member administers, returning one row per page mailbox with its mailbox_urn (urn:li:fsd_pageMailbox:<id>), company_urn (the owning urn:li:fsd_company:<id>) and messaging_enabled flag. Read-only, safe to retry, and cheap to call; it does not include the member's personal inbox, and a pageMailbox urn cannot be used where send_message expects a urn:li:fsd_profile:… personal mailbox_urn.

actions.name: list_people_at_company
actions.description: Lists people who work at a given LinkedIn company, paginated at 12 per page by default, returning one row per person with name, headline, location, profile_url, profile_urn, degree (DISTANCE_1/2/3, OUT_OF_NETWORK, SELF) and total (the full result set size, repeated on every row). Read-only and safe to retry; to filter by name or role within the company use search_people_at_company instead.

actions.name: list_shared_connections
actions.description: Lists LinkedIn mutual connections (1st-degree connections of both you and another member), 10 per page, with name, headline, location, public profile URL, profile_urn and degree. Read-only and safe to retry; capped at 1000 rows and limited to people within your network reach.

actions.name: reject_invitation
actions.description: Declines a pending LinkedIn connection invitation by sending the same ignore action as the UI's dismiss button; this changes state on the user's LinkedIn account immediately and the sender is not notified. The user must approve this action before it is called, and the inputs must come from a list_invitations call made immediately beforehand.

invitation_id.description: Identifier of the pending invitation to decline, taken from the list_invitations result.

validation_token.description: Single-use validation token for this invitation from the list_invitations result read immediately beforehand; it cannot be reused, so re-list if it fails.

profile_id.description: Identifier of the inviting member's profile, taken from the same list_invitations entry as the invitation.

_payload.value: ["Sorry, invitation from Jai not ignored. Please try again."]

actions.name: search_companies
actions.description: Search LinkedIn for companies by name or keyword (Companies tab of search results, 10 per page). Returns each match's name, industry, city, followers, company page URL, numeric company id and logo paths; use it to resolve a company before calling get_company. Read-only and safe to retry.

keywords.description: Company name or keyword to search for, e.g. "Microsoft".

actions.name: search_companies_and_people
actions.description: Fast LinkedIn typeahead that resolves a person or company name to suggestions, including the numeric company id (from tracking_urn) used by other company tools; it does not return the universalName slug (use search_companies for that). Read-only and safe to retry, it returns only a few results by design.

actions.name: search_jobs_at_company
actions.description: List open LinkedIn job postings at a given company within a required country or city geography, returning one row per posting (title, job_urn, reposted flag, and total open postings) at 10 per page. This is a read-only operation and is safe to retry.

company_id.description: LinkedIn numeric company ID, obtained from search_companies_and_people or search_companies (e.g. "1035").

geo_id.description: Required LinkedIn geography ID for a country or city (e.g. "103644278" for United States, "101165590" for United Kingdom). There is no worldwide option; if omitted or invalid, LinkedIn silently falls back to the member's own country.

actions.name: search_people
actions.description: Search for people on the professional networking platform by keywords, returning matching profiles with name, headline, location, current or past position, connection degree, profile URL and image links, and mutual connections. This is a read-only operation that changes no data and is safe to retry. Fields: name (else name_2, else name_3), headline, location, current_or_past_position, connection_degree (' • 2nd'), profile_id (ACoAA…), profile_url (else profile_url_2, a relative /in/<slug>/). The vanity_name for get_profile / send_connection_request is the <slug> in the profile link.

keywords.description: Free-text search query, such as a person's name plus an employer, school, or other identifying terms (e.g. "yuzhong luo oxford").

actions.name: search_people_at_company
actions.description: Search LinkedIn for people at a specific company using a company filter plus free-text keywords matched against names and headlines, returning one row per person (name, headline, location, profile_url, profile_urn, degree, total) at 12 per page. This is read-only and safe to retry; to search all of LinkedIn use search_people instead.

company_id.description: LinkedIn numeric company ID to search within, e.g. "1035". Obtain it from search_companies_and_people or search_companies.

keywords.description: Free-text keywords matched against people's names and headlines, e.g. "engineer".

actions.name: send_connection_request
actions.description: Sends a LinkedIn connection request to the member identified by their profile vanity name. This changes state on the user's account by creating a pending invitation, so the user must explicitly approve it before the tool is called.

vanity_name.description: The target member's LinkedIn vanity name, which is the slug after /in/ in their profile URL (e.g. 'jane-doe-123').

actions.name: send_message
actions.description: Sends a real LinkedIn message into an existing conversation thread on the user's account; it is delivered to the recipient immediately and cannot be unsent. This changes account state, so the user must approve it before you call it. It cannot start a new thread, and it returns the created message's URN and echoed body.

text.description: The message body to send to the recipient, exactly as it should appear. Confirm the wording with the user before sending.

conversation_urn.description: URN of the existing LinkedIn conversation thread to send the message into. A new thread cannot be created with this tool.
